name: ARPANET networked electronic mail
description: An early networked messaging implementation sent mail between TENEX users on separate ARPANET-connected hosts using recipient and host addressing.

impact.note: Mail between separate networked computers was a new way to communicate; Internet mail descended from it and many societies came to depend on it.

date.basis: Date or approximate interval stated by the source for this event.

events.statement: Ray Tomlinson demonstrated networked mail between two TENEX systems connected to the ARPANET in 1971.

evidence.supports: The history attributes implementation and address separator to Tomlinson.
Participant-based history describes the implementation, addressing and demonstration.

date.label: early 1972 (approximate)
date.basis: Date or approximate interval stated by the source for this event.

events.statement: Tomlinson recalled use of network mail among ARPANET collaborators in early 1972.
events.caveats: The participant estimate of possible users is approximate and is not a measured adoption figure.

evidence.supports: Tomlinson recalls use across the limited ARPANET community.

earliest_record.rationale: Earliest dated event established in the cited sources for this scoped record; it does not assert global priority.

caveats: Local mailbox systems, including CTSS, existed earlier; the demonstration is one networked implementation, not the origin of all electronic messaging.

research.note: Source-backed initial research; independent review is pending.
